1. BMC Med Res Methodol. 2012 Jul 7;12:95. doi: 10.1186/1471-2288-12-95.

Simultaneous evaluation of abstinence and relapse using a Markov chain model in 
smokers enrolled in a two-year randomized trial.

Yeh HW(1), Ellerbeck EF, Mahnken JD.

Author information:
(1)Department of Biostatistics, The University of Kansas Medical Center, Kansas 
City, KS 66160, USA. hyeh@kumc.edu

BACKGROUND: GEE and mixed models are powerful tools to compare treatment effects 
in longitudinal smoking cessation trials. However, they are not capable of 
assessing the relapse (from abstinent back to smoking) simultaneously with 
cessation, which can be studied by transition models.
METHODS: We apply a first-order Markov chain model to analyze the transition of 
smoking status measured every 6 months in a 2-year randomized smoking cessation 
trial, and to identify what factors are associated with the transition from 
smoking to abstinent and from abstinent to smoking. Missing values due to 
non-response are assumed non-ignorable and handled by the selection modeling 
approach.
RESULTS: Smokers receiving high-intensity disease management (HDM), of male 
gender, lower daily cigarette consumption, higher motivation and confidence to 
quit, and having serious attempts to quit were more likely to become abstinent 
(OR = 1.48, 1.66, 1.03, 1.15, 1.09 and 1.34, respectively) in the next 6 months. 
Among those who were abstinent, lower income and stronger nicotine dependence 
(OR = 1.72 for ≤ vs. > 40 K and OR = 1.75 for first cigarette ≤ vs. > 5 min) 
were more likely to have relapse in the next 6 months.
CONCLUSIONS: Markov chain models allow investigation of dynamic 
smoking-abstinence behavior and suggest that relapse is influenced by different 
factors than cessation. The knowledge of treatments and covariates in 
transitions in both directions may provide guidance for designing more effective 
interventions on smoking cessation and relapse prevention.

DOI: 10.1186/1471-2288-12-95
PMCID: PMC3
